prompt: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite concept for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: a single STEED FOAL enemy of the Iron Tide, a small homing seahorse-shaped drone, isolated. An upright mechanical seahorse built from riveted overlapping steel-blue plates with cool gray highlights, an arched neck bending forward, a short tube snout pointing left with a warm amber face-lamp glowing at its tip, and a small dark visor eye. A ridged dorsal fin on its back and two little side fins with tiny white-violet static spark ticks crackling at their edges. Its lower body tapers into a segmented cable tail that curls into a tight spiral beneath it. A bit taller than wide, a clean question-mark silhouette. Side view facing left, centered with a generous empty margin on all sides on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background that fills the whole image. Crisp chunky pixel art with a 1-pixel near-black navy outline at the sprite's native pixel scale, flat saturated fills with three-step shading ramps lit from the top-left, bold simple shape that stays readable at small size, no anti-aliasing, no water, no bubbles, no scenery, no stars, no cast shadow, no glow bleeding onto the background, no text, no labels.
